# Whether a ball contains another, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_contains_ball_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$, $X$ the ball of center $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$ and radius $r_y$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies Y \subseteq X.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true only if $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$.
- When an operand is the empty set or the whole line, it is true exactly then.
- For finite operands it may be false although the relation holds, close to where it stops holding: the answer is certain, not exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_contains_ball_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_contains_ball_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** an upper bound of the distance of the centers by add_ball_2_2 and radd, compared with the radius (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`abs_upper_2`](abs_upper_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md).

```
# Whether a ball with a 2-limb center contains another, Y inside X (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", the row of contains(Y): certain): with (z, e) = add_ball_2_2(c_y, -c_x), hi =
# radd(abs_upper_2(z), e) is at least |c_y - c_x|, and s = radd(hi, r_y) at least |c_y - c_x| + r_y;
# the answer is s <= r_x, which implies the containment. The special states as for one limb: true
# when X is the whole line or Y is empty; the comparison gives false for an empty X and a nonempty Y
# and for a whole line Y in a finite X (s is then +inf). Certain, not exact: undecided within about
# e and a step of T of the boundary.

ncx0        = neg(cx0)
ncx1        = neg(cx1)
(z0, z1, e) = add_ball_2_2(cy0, cy1, ncx0, ncx1)
au          = abs_upper_2(z0, z1)
hi          = radd(au, e)
s           = radd(hi, ry)
f           = le(s, rx)
wx          = eq(rx, const inf)
qy          = eq(ry, ry)
ey          = not(qy)
sp          = or(wx, ey)
m           = or(sp, f)
```
